latest_release.name: v0.9.5
latest_release.body:
This is a hotfix release for v0.9.4. See the v0.9.4 notes for the full feature release: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tag/v0.9.4

### Fixed
- Prefix shortcuts work again when the terminal sends the next key as plain text. This affected Tern, Chinese, Japanese and Korean input methods on macOS, and Ghostty `text:` keybinds that send the prefix and a key together. Workspace navigation had the same problem. (#5255)
- Codex sessions no longer start with a "clamping Interrupt hook timeout" warning. Herdr no longer installs Codex turn hooks, and Codex status comes from screen detection again. Run `herdr integration install codex` to update. (#5246, #5278)
- Claude Code questions show as blocked in named sessions. (#4573, #5192)
- On Windows, plugin panes start even when a folder on `PATH` has the same name as the plugin's program. (#5267, #5269, thanks @JJLiebig)
- On Windows, Claude Code session tracking works when the user folder name contains non-ASCII characters, such as Korean. (#5253, #5270, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Adding a Windows machine no longer prints raw PowerShell progress output. (#4639, #5282, thanks @JJLiebig)

hot_issues.title: macOS: herdr server has no grantable app identity, so panes lose Local Network access and TCC consent (live-handoff, remote attach, detached daemon)
Agent detection misses nix-wrapped Claude Code (.claude-unwrapped); devenv agents never appear in the agent panel
Keystrokes tear frames from TUIs that use synchronized output
Neovim colored underlines render incorrectly in Herdr compared with Kitty/tmux
Codex 0.157 shared daemon breaks per-pane sessions and HERDR_* env (waiting on upstream)
Prime Agent built-in herdr reporter: state reports work, session/identity don't (evidence + request)
Running multiple agents simultaneously causes severe lag, high resource usage, and noisy fans on macOS after upgrading to v0.8.2
Grok: Shift+Enter does not insert newline inside herdr pane (Ghostty host); Alt+Enter works

discussions.title: Read-only authoritative activity for an existing live agent instance
[idea] Herdr app: turn off the frame on a lone pane without leaving the shipped layout
Per-agent colors in the collapsed Agent sidebar
Kitty graphics: images don't render on Windows when the sender uses file-path transmission (t=f); direct transmission (t=d) works
Open a forked agent session in its own tab (and background sessions bind the wrong pane)
Let a socket focus request target one client (workspace.focus / tab.focus for the caller), not every attached client
[idea] Drop a file from Finder onto a terminal pane in the Herdr app to paste its path
[idea] Per-agent sound files (done_path / request_path for each agent)

# herdr

--- https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/043ec09f-4bdd-41d5-aee0-8fda6b83e267 **the runtime your coding agents live on.** - **detach without stopping work** — herdr keeps terminals running in a background server when you close the client or lose your SSH connection. after a server or machine restart, herdr restores the saved layout and can resume supported agent sessions; the original processes do not survive. [session state →](https://herdr.dev/docs/session-state/) - **several machines, one window** — keep local work and saved ssh machines together, with a combined agent list and independent reconnects. [remote machines →](https://herdr.dev/docs/connecting-machines/) - **never hunt for the stuck one** — every pane is marked working, blocked, or idle. when an agent stops and needs an answer, herdr says so. - **agent-native** — agents drive herdr through the cli and socket api: they can spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is genuinely blocked. [agent skill →](https://herdr.dev/docs/agent-skill/) - **runs what you already run** — claude code, codex, cursor, opencode, grok and the rest. herdr doesn't wrap or replace them; it owns their terminals. building an agent? [add herdr support →](https://herdr.dev/docs/add-herdr-support/) - **keyboard and mouse, both first-class** — tmux-style prefix keys *and* click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool. - **plugins** — extend panes and workflows.
